title: Birbal counts the crows.
lines: Long ago in India there lived a great emperor.
His name was Akbar.
He lived in a beautiful palace of red stone, with towers and gardens and fountains.
Emperor Akbar had a best friend.
That was Birbal.
Birbal was the cleverest man in the whole empire.
He had an answer for every question.
Emperor Akbar liked asking Birbal difficult questions.
Questions that nobody could really answer.
He wanted to see if Birbal would ever say: I don't know.
One warm afternoon they were walking together in the palace garden.
The flowers smelled lovely.
The peacocks strutted around proudly.
And there were lots and lots of crows in the trees.
Black crows, cawing away.
Caw!
Caw!
Caw!
Emperor Akbar looked at the crows.
He had an idea.
He smiled.
Birbal, he said, I have a question for you.
How many crows are there in our whole city?
All the courtiers walking with them looked at each other.
What a difficult question!
Nobody can count all the crows!
They fly around all the time.
They thought: Now Birbal won't know for once.
But Birbal thought for a moment.
He stroked his beard.
He looked at the sky.
Then he said very calmly: There are ninety-one thousand, four hundred and twelve crows in our city, Your Majesty.
Emperor Akbar frowned.
That many?
he said.
Are you sure?
Very sure, said Birbal.
If you don't believe me, Your Majesty, you can have them counted.
The emperor laughed.
But Birbal, he said, what if my men count them and there are fewer?
What then?
Then, said Birbal, some of the crows are on holiday.
They're visiting their family in another city.
The courtiers had to laugh.
And if there are more?
asked the emperor.
Then, said Birbal with a wink, our crows have visitors: their cousins from other cities.
Because crows love a party too!
Now Emperor Akbar laughed so hard that he had to hold his tummy.
He laughed so loudly that the peacocks got a fright.
Ha ha ha!
Birbal, you're impossible!
You always have an answer!
He clapped Birbal on the shoulder.
But then he became serious again.
Birbal, he said, tell me honestly.
Do you really know how many crows there are?
Birbal laughed.
No, Your Majesty, he said.
Nobody knows that.
But you asked a question that has no real answer.
So I gave you an answer that nobody can check.
And it was a funny answer.
Sometimes that's clever too.
The emperor nodded.
You're right, he said.
Some questions aren't there to find an answer.
They're there to laugh a little and to think.
As a reward the emperor gave Birbal a beautiful gold ring.
And that evening he had lots of grain scattered in the garden.
For all the crows in the city, he said.
And for their cousins too.
The crows all came.
Caw!
Caw!
Caw!
They pecked up the grain.
Birbal and the emperor sat on a bench and watched.
Shall we count them after all?
asked the emperor.
One, two, three, four...
Birbal laughed.
Then we'll still be at it next year, Your Majesty!
And they laughed together, as the sun went down behind the red palace.
The end.
